answer: Resist sybils via unique archive custody: each vault at registration is VRF-assigned one disjoint 64 MB shard of the ledger's relic archive; no two vaults share bytes. Each epoch validators fire byte-range proofs; a shard returning hollow means a 10% stake slash by the settlement contract. Cost per identity: one shard plus 10% slash risk; shards are content-disjoint, so n identities need n stores, marginal cost linear in n. Splitting cannot reset this: shard bytes are pinned to each vault's registration hash. Like timber framing, a missing beam fails inspection.
